attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, rejecting a hypothetical he sets up himself.

semantics.note: 'It will not!' is a firm negative forecast that the government will not fund these companies forever. The 'even if' is a rhetorical setup, not an antecedent. No deadline is given.

contract.note: Reading 'forever' as open-ended support that keeps these firms alive, and excluding ordinary procurement, is a fair and ordinary reading. Only an implemented open-ended rescue could settle it early, and that would contradict it.

evidence.note: GSA disclosure (agency, not company) of a finite, consumption-based procurement deal with no spending commitment. This is ordinary purchasing, not a rescue.
Reuters, Nov 2025: Sacks said there would be no federal AI bailout. This is a statement of intent and cannot settle an open-ended forecast.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. The packet shows no implemented open-ended federal rescue by the cutoff, so the contradiction condition is not met. A finite record also cannot establish that such support will never happen. The evidence does not settle it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion: 'we haven't had one'.

semantics.note: The rhetorical question is followed by a firm statement that none has existed. The exclusions for training-data firms and Nvidia are preserved. The contract correctly reads 'haven't had one' as cumulative.

contract.note: Calendar 2022 through publication is a reasonable stand-in for 'three years in'. The speaker named no profit measure. The contract requires the meaning of profitability to be established and bars a firm verdict on an unknown accounting basis.

evidence.note: Midjourney's founder told The Register in 2022 that the company was 'already profitable'. This is self-reported with no defined measure, so it points against the claim but is not an established finding.
HeyGen's own 2024 post says it has been profitable since Q2 2023. This is a company disclosure with no defined profit basis.

reviews.rationale: Two generative AI firms outside the exclusions said they were profitable within the period. That strongly challenges the claim. But both are undefined self-reports, and the contract requires profitability to be established on a known basis. The packet therefore does not firmly settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own prediction in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The surrounding text ('popping of the AI bubble', 'Expect to see') makes the bubble's collapse the antecedent. The 'will' consequences are firm. 'Grim' is emphasis.

contract.note: Reading 'drying-up' as a severe, broad contraction, and requiring pension losses to reach retirees' spending, is fair and ordinary. The contract requires a dated bust to be established first.

evidence.note: J.P. Morgan, Oct 2026: AI took most venture funding and other startups face selective funding. It shows concentration, not a collapse after a bust.
CalPERS self-reported a strong FY2025-26 return. This is one fund, before any trigger, so it does not test the conditional.
UK regulator guidance on AI concentration risk. It is a risk warning, not evidence of losses, and has UK scope.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not show that the AI bubble has popped, so the antecedent is unknown and the conditional cannot be scored. The evidence shows no post-bust venture collapse and no pension losses reaching retirees.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words, repeating what he says he wrote before.

semantics.note: The main claim is that Stargate does not exist beyond hype. The drafter turned 'isn't saving it' into 'won't save', a small tense change. That part has no measure and is not separately scored.

contract.note: Reading Stargate as OpenAI's branded infrastructure program and 'exists' as real construction is the ordinary reading. A narrower reading, the SoftBank joint venture, is plausible and is flagged. The choice of reading decides the result.

evidence.note: OpenAI's July 22, 2025 disclosure says Stargate I in Abilene was under construction and partly running workloads. This is a company disclosure, which the contract prefers for project status.
Bisnow, citing WSJ: the SoftBank joint venture had closed no deals, which fits the narrow reading. It also confirms Abilene was being built under the Stargate name.

reviews.rationale: On the contract's ordinary reading, infrastructure named Stargate was being built and partly operating before publication. Both OpenAI's disclosure and independent reporting say so, which defeats 'doesn't exist beyond hype'. The joint venture's stall supports only a narrower reading. 'Isn't saving it' cannot be measured.
